To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dendritic cells (a type of immune cell) were stimulated to become more active by a streptococcal product (OK432) and were then injected into tumours during transcatheter hepatectomy.

OK432‐stimulation of DCs promotes their maturation towards activated cells with tumoricidal activity and that infusion of these OK432‐stimu‐lated DCs into tumour tissues during TAE treatment exerts beneficial anti-tumour effects against HCC.

the infusion of OK432‐activated dendritic cells into hepatocellular tumours following hepatic arterial chemoembolization treatment prolongs the time to tumour recurrence in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the safety and feasibility of OK432‐activated dendritic cells (OK432‐DCs) as a potential immunotherapeutic agent for patients with HCC undergoing TAE.
the safety and feasibility of OK432‐induced dendritic cell transfer in patients with hepatitis C‐associated hepatocellular carcinoma.

the results obtained with this study are very encouraging.
the combination of TAE and DC infusion may be beneficial for HCC treatment.
the use of OK432‐activated DCs is a feasible and safe immunotherapeutic strategy that may be used as an adjuvant treatment for HCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

OK432‐stimulation of immature DCs promotes their maturation and activation towards cells with tumoricidal capacity, which can be safely administered into tumour tissues of patients with HCC during TAE.
the OK432‐stimulating DC transfer into tumour tissue during TAE treatment may be a feasible and safe strategy for the treatment of patients with HCC.
OK432‐stimulation of DCs promotes their maturation towards activated cells and enhances their immunomodulatory activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DC‐based active immunotherapy is a feasible and safe strategy to enhance the anti‐tumoral effects of locoregional therapy in HCC.
the combination of DCs with OK432 and TAE may be an effective treatment for HCC, and that the combination of OK432 and TAA may be an effective strategy for other solid tumors as well.

OK432‐stimulation of DCs promotes their maturation towards activated cells with enhanced immunomodulatory properties, and that infusion of these cells into tumour tissues during TAE treatment is feasible and safe.
